newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia pushes for high-growth exports to Japan.
newsitem.headline: Australia pushes for high-growth exports to Japan.

text.p: The Australian government urged its exporters on Monday to focus on selling high-growth products to Japan in order to turn around Australia's falling status as a Japanese trading partner.

Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer said Australia's fall from the third largest supplier of Japanese imports in 1994 to sixth largest this year was mainly due to Australia concentrating on the low-growth end of Japan's import boom.
"The challenge for Australian firms therefore is to increase exports in the high growth areas of Japanese markets," Fischer told a luncheon of Australian and Japanese economic and security analysts.

"Potential high-growth sectors where Australian excels include processed food, housing and construction, transport equipment, such as hi-tech ferries, cars and autoparts, telecommunications and services," said Fischer, who is also trade minister.
Australia's enormous exports of bulk, unprocessed commodities -- especially coal and iron ore -- make it one of the few countries that runs a trade surplus with Japan.
Australian exports to Japan were worth A$16.4 billion (US$12.7 billion) in the year to June 1996 compared with imports of A$10.8 billion.
But Fischer said some Australian businesses had recently begun to view Japan as a difficult market.

"Some companies have formed a view that the economic difficulties of the past five years -- and there has been a degree of softening in the economic growth in Japan, together with market access problems, high market entry and running costs -- make Japan too tough a market to tackle," Fischer said.
"I do not subscribe to that view," he said.

Fischer said Japan's economic recovery now looked sustainable and recent structural reforms had begun to have an impact. "Some of the barriers to market access in key areas for Australian exporters are less formidable," he said.
Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto is due to visit Australia on April 28 and 29.
